ap_macroeconomics-m01.stem: Which statement correctly compares the effects of a dollar appreciation and a dollar depreciation on U.S. net exports?

options.text: Neither changes net exports, because trade depends only on incomes and not on prices.
options.why: Relative prices expressed in a common currency affect trade.

options.text: An appreciation makes U.S. exports cheaper and imports more expensive, which raises net exports.
options.why: This is the effect of a depreciation, not an appreciation.

options.text: An appreciation makes U.S. exports more expensive and imports cheaper, which lowers net exports, while a depreciation has the opposite effect.
options.why: A stronger dollar buys more foreign currency, so U.S. goods cost more abroad and foreign goods cost less in the United States.

options.text: Both an appreciation and a depreciation raise net exports, because exchange rate changes help trade in both directions.
options.why: The two changes move net exports in opposite directions.

options.text: A depreciation lowers net exports, because the dollar buys less foreign currency.
options.why: A depreciation lowers the foreign price of U.S. goods and raises net exports.

ap_macroeconomics-m02.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes a trade deficit from a budget deficit?

options.text: A trade deficit means exports exceed imports, while a budget deficit means tax revenue exceeds spending.
options.why: Both definitions are reversed; these describe a trade surplus and a budget surplus.

options.text: A trade deficit means government spending exceeds tax revenue, while a budget deficit means imports exceed exports.
options.why: This swaps the two definitions.

options.text: A trade deficit means imports exceed exports, while a budget deficit means government spending exceeds tax revenue.
options.why: A trade deficit is about trade with the rest of the world; a budget deficit is about the government's own finances.

options.text: A trade deficit and a budget deficit are the same thing, because both mean spending exceeds income.
options.why: They measure different flows and can move independently.

options.text: A trade deficit measures the total national debt, while a budget deficit measures the interest on the debt.
options.why: Neither is a measure of the debt or of its interest.
